resumen: How nouns, adjectives, verbs and adverbs are formed from a root with prefixes and suffixes. It greatly expands your vocabulary and helps you recognise new words.

explicacion.texto: One root gives a whole family: employ (verb), employment / employer / employee (nouns), unemployed (adjective). Knowing which word class the sentence needs (is a noun missing? an adjective?) is half the work.

filas: develop → development; decide → decision; perform → performance
nation → national; economy → economic; effect → effective; danger → dangerous
modern → modernise; wide → widen; simple → simplify

items: Spelling changes: happy → happiness (y → i), argue → argument (the e is dropped), begin → beginning (double consonant).
im- before p/m/b (impossible), il- before l (illegal), ir- before r (irregular).

ejemplos.frase: The employer must pay its employees on time.
ejemplos.traduccion: El empleador debe pagar puntualmente a sus empleados.

ejemplos.frase: Housing is becoming less and less affordable for young people.
ejemplos.traduccion: La vivienda es cada vez menos asequible para los jóvenes.

ejemplos.frase: I think you have misunderstood the question.
ejemplos.traduccion: Creo que has entendido mal la pregunta.

ejemplos.frase: Nurses are often overworked and underpaid.
ejemplos.traduccion: Las enfermeras suelen estar sobrecargadas de trabajo y mal pagadas.

ejemplos.frase: The campaign raised awareness of the problem.
ejemplos.traduccion: La campaña concienció sobre el problema.

ejemplos.frase: Parking here is illegal after 8 p.m.
ejemplos.traduccion: Aparcar aquí es ilegal después de las ocho de la tarde.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Before p, the negative prefix is im-.
“Economic” = related to the economy; “economical” = saving money.
English adjectives have no plural form.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: The ___ of the new hospital took three years. (construct)
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row of the suffix table for -ment, -tion / -sion, which form nouns of action or state. The clue is the article the before the gap and the preposition of after it: a noun is needed, and it is also the subject of took. The verb construct gives construction, “the act of building”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After “the” a noun is needed: construction.
ejercicios.traduccion: La construcción del nuevo hospital llevó tres años.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The -ing form can work as a noun, but after the and with of the proper noun is construction.
Construct does not form its noun with -ment but with -tion: construction.
A constructor is the person or company that builds; here we are talking about the action: construction.

glosario.definicion_l: the act of constructing something · a group of words that form a constituent of a sentence and are considered as a single unit

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: Flats in the city centre are no longer ___ for most families. (afford)
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the -able / -ible row of the table, which forms adjectives meaning “that can be done”. The clue is are no longer ___ for: after the verb be an adjective is needed. Afford means “to be able to pay for” and affordable means “that you can pay for, reasonably priced” (es: asequible).
ejercicios.traduccion: Los pisos del centro de la ciudad ya no son asequibles para la mayoría de las familias.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Afford is spelt with a double f and keeps it: affordable.
With afford the suffix is -able: affordable.
Affordability is the noun; after are the adjective affordable is needed.

glosario.definicion_l: that you have the financial means for
not now

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row of the table with the suffixes for people: -er / -or, -ee, -ist. The clue is 500 before the gap: a plural noun for people is needed. -ee refers to the person who receives the action (the employee) and -er to the person who performs it (the employer), so the word is employees.
ejercicios.traduccion: La empresa tiene 500 empleados en España.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Employers are the people who hire; the people hired are employees.
With 500 the plural is needed: employees.
Employment is the situation of having a job, not the person; the people are employees.

glosario.definicion_l: a worker who is hired to perform a job
a person or firm that employs workers
the state of being employed or having a job · the occupation for which you are paid

ejercicios.frase: It is ___legal to drive without insurance.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule from the Rules and key points list: il- before l. The clue is that the root legal begins with l, so the negative prefix in- assimilates and becomes il-: illegal, with a double l. The same happens in Spanish (“ilegal”), although with a single l.

por_opcion.il: Correct: before l the negative prefix is il-: illegal.
por_opcion.un: Incorrect: un- is the most general negative prefix (unfair), but legal takes the Latin variant il-.
por_opcion.in: Incorrect: in- becomes il- before l; “inlegal” does not exist.
por_opcion.dis: Incorrect: dis- expresses the opposite with verbs and some adjectives (dishonest), but it does not form “dislegal”.

glosario.definicion_l: prohibited by law or by official or accepted rules

promise of reimbursement in the case of loss; paid to people or companies so concerned about hazards that they have made prepayments to an insurance company · written contract or certificate of insurance

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the -ly row of the table, which forms adverbs from adjectives. The clue is that the gap modifies the verb have risen (how they have risen): an adverb is needed, not an adjective. Significant + -ly gives significantly, “notably, considerably”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It modifies a verb: the -ly adverb is needed.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los precios han subido considerablemente desde enero.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Significant is an adjective and cannot modify a verb; the adverb significantly is needed.
Significance is the noun (“importance”); the verb needs an adverb.
-ly is added directly: significantly, without an e.

glosario.definicion_l: in a statistically significant way · in a significant manner

ejercicios.frase: I'm afraid I completely ___ what you said.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the mis- row of the prefix table: “badly, wrongly”. The clue is I'm afraid and completely: the speaker admits a misunderstanding. Mis- + understood gives misunderstood, “understood wrongly”. The other prefixes do not combine with understand.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me temo que he entendido completamente mal lo que dijiste.

por_opcion.disunderstood: Incorrect: dis- does not combine with understand; it is a copy of other negative prefixes.
por_opcion.ununderstood: Incorrect: un- does not form the negative of this verb; this word does not exist.
por_opcion.overunderstood: Incorrect: over- means “too much” (overestimate), and “understand too much” makes no sense.

ejercicios.frase: Living here without a car is almost unpossible.
respuestas: Living here without a car is almost impossible.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule from Rules and key points: im- before p, m or b. The clue is that possible begins with p, so the negative prefix is im-: impossible. It is the typical mistake listed in this unit (unpossible), caused by overusing the prefix un-.
ejercicios.traduccion: Vivir aquí sin coche es casi imposible.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Living here without a car is almost unpossible.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: before p the negative prefix is im-.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Living here without a car is almost inpossible.
errores_previstos.explicacion: In- becomes im- before p: impossible.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Living here without a car is almost imposible.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish spelling; in English it is spelt with a double s: impossible.

glosario.definicion_l: not capable of occurring or being accomplished or dealt with · totally unlikely
(of actions or states) slightly short of or not quite accomplished; all but

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: Her ___ to speak five languages impressed everyone. (able)
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the -ity, -ness row of the table: nouns of quality. The clue is the possessive her before the gap, which requires a noun, the subject of impressed. Able (capable) gives ability (capacity), with a spelling change: able loses the -e and becomes -bil-.
ejercicios.traduccion: Su capacidad para hablar cinco idiomas impresionó a todos.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Able does not form its noun with -ness; the form is ability.
An i is missing: ability.
Able is the adjective (“capable”); after the possessive her the noun ability is needed.

glosario.definicion_l: the quality of being able to perform; a quality that permits or facilitates achievement or accomplishment · possession of the qualities (especially mental qualities) required to do something or get something done

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: The government wants to ___ the tax system. (simple)
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the -ise / -ize, -en, -ify row of the table, which forms verbs. The clue is wants to ___: after to an infinitive is needed. Simple + -ify gives simplify, “make simpler”, losing the final -e.
ejercicios.traduccion: El Gobierno quiere simplificar el sistema tributario.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A copy of Spanish “simplificar”; the English verb is simplify.
Simple does not form its verb with -ise but with -ify: simplify.
This is the noun; after wants to the verb simplify is needed.

glosario.definicion_l: a legal system for assessing and collecting taxes

ejercicios.frase: Many young people are ___ and run their own businesses.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the self- row of the prefix table (es: auto-). The clue is the second part, run their own businesses: someone who runs their own business works for themselves, that is, they are self-employed (es: autónomo). It is a very common term in texts on labour economics.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Someone who has their own business is “self-employed” (es: autónomo).
ejercicios.traduccion: Muchos jóvenes son autónomos y llevan su propio negocio.

por_opcion.self-employed: Correct: self-employed = working for yourself (es: autónomo).
por_opcion.unemployed: Incorrect: unemployed means “without a job”; it contradicts run their own businesses.
por_opcion.employers: Incorrect: employers are people who hire others; it would be grammatical, but it does not describe someone who works for themselves, who may have no employees at all.
por_opcion.employable: Incorrect: employable means “suitable to be hired”.

glosario.definicion_l: working for yourself
not engaged in a gainful occupation · people who are involuntarily out of work (considered as a group)

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: Thank you for your ___ during the move. (help)
ejercicios.explicacion: The general rule of this unit is to identify the word class the sentence needs. The clue is the possessive your: a noun is needed. Here the noun is the same as the verb (help), with no suffix; helpfulness (kindness, willingness to help), derived with -ful and -ness, is also accepted. It is a good reminder that you do not always have to add a suffix.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A noun is needed here, and it is the same as the verb: help.
ejercicios.traduccion: Gracias por tu ayuda durante la mudanza.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Helpful is an adjective (“useful, willing to help”); after your a noun is needed.
Your helping is not natural here; the noun is help.
This word does not exist; help already works as a noun.

glosario.definicion_l: the activity of contributing to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose · a person who contributes to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose
the property of providing useful assistance · friendliness evidence by a kindly and helpful disposition
the act of deciding to do something · the act of changing your residence or place of business

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: That's a very ___ suggestion; thank you. (use)
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the -ful, -less row of the table: adjectives meaning “with” and “without”. The clue is a very ___ suggestion: between very and the noun an adjective is needed, and the thanks show a positive opinion. Use + -ful gives useful; useless would be the opposite.
ejercicios.traduccion: Es una sugerencia muy útil; gracias.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Useless means “of no use”; it contradicts thank you.
The suffix -ful is spelt with a single l: useful.
Usable means “that can be used” (in working order); for a valuable suggestion we say useful.

glosario.definicion_l: being of use or service · having a useful function
an idea that is suggested · a proposal offered for acceptance or rejection

ejercicios.frase: The economical crisis lasted almost six years.
respuestas: The economic crisis lasted almost six years.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the typical mistake listed in this unit: economic means “related to the economy” and economical means “saving money, cheap”. The clue is the noun crisis: it is a crisis of the economy, so the adjective is economic. Both have suffixes from the table (-ic and -al), but their meanings are different.
ejercicios.traduccion: La crisis económica duró casi seis años.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The economical crisis lasted almost six years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: economical means “saving money”; a crisis of the economy is economic.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The economics crisis lasted almost six years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Economics is the science of economics; the adjective is economic.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The economy crisis lasted almost six years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Economy is the noun; before crisis the natural choice is the adjective economic.

glosario.definicion_l: of or relating to an economy, the system of production and management of material wealth · of or relating to the science of economics
using the minimum of time or resources necessary for effectiveness · of or relating to an economy, the system of production and management of material wealth

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: Workers in this sector are badly ___. (pay)
ejercicios.explicacion: The general rule of this unit is to identify the word class: after are badly a participle used as an adjective is needed. The clue is the adverb badly, which modifies a participle: badly paid, “not paid enough”. Pay is irregular and its participle is paid, not “payed”. The table also includes underpaid, which says the same with the prefix under-.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Participle of “pay”: paid (badly paid = es: mal pagado).
ejercicios.traduccion: Los trabajadores de este sector están mal pagados.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Pay is irregular: the participle is paid.
After are with a passive meaning the participle is needed: paid.
Are paying would be active (“they are paying”); the workers receive the pay: paid.

ejercicios.frase: The ministers agreed to ___ the decision next month.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the re- row of the prefix table: “again”. The clue is the decision already taken and next month: it will be examined again. Reconsider means “think about again, review”. The other prefixes do not combine with consider.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los ministros acordaron reconsiderar la decisión el mes que viene.

por_opcion.preconsider: Incorrect: pre- means “before”, but preconsider is not a word used in English.
por_opcion.misconsider: Incorrect: mis- means “wrongly”, but misconsider does not exist.
por_opcion.unconsider: Incorrect: un- does not form verbs from consider; this word does not exist.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: The new manager made the team much more ___. (effect)
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the -al, -ic, -ive, -ous row of the table, which forms adjectives. The clue is the structure make + object + adjective (made the team more ___): an adjective is needed. Effect + -ive gives effective, “producing the intended result” (es: eficaz). Do not confuse it with efficient (not wasting resources).
ejercicios.traduccion: El nuevo director hizo que el equipo fuera mucho más eficaz.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Effectively is an adverb; after make + object an adjective is needed: effective.
Effective is spelt with a double f.
This is the noun (“effectiveness”); the structure made the team more needs an adjective.

glosario.definicion_l: producing or capable of producing an intended result or having a striking effect · able to accomplish a purpose; functioning effectively
someone who controls resources and expenditures · (sports) someone in charge of training an athlete or a team

descripcion_larga_es: Word formation explains how an English root gives rise to a family of nouns, adjectives, verbs and adverbs through prefixes and suffixes: employ, employment, employer, employee, unemployed. Mastering it multiplies your vocabulary, helps you work out the meaning of new words in a text and avoids word-class or prefix mistakes (unpossible, economical for economic) that are common among Spanish speakers.

contexto.que_es: It is the English system of derivation: suffixes change the word class (develop → development, rapid → rapidly) and prefixes change the meaning (fair → unfair, understand → misunderstand, consider → reconsider). It includes the variants of the negative prefix (im-, il-, ir-) and the spelling changes when suffixes are added.
contexto.por_que_importa: It lets you recognise and produce many words from a few roots, which is essential for reading economic or legal texts fluently. It is also a classic exercise type in English exams (complete with the correct form of the word). Mistakes in this area, such as an adjective where an adverb belongs or economical for economic, are very noticeable and sometimes change the meaning.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It applies whenever a sentence needs a specific word class: after an article, a noun; before a noun or after be, an adjective; modifying a verb, an adverb. Those are the signals to look for. Spanish speakers tend to copy Spanish prefixes and suffixes (unpossible, responsable) or to confuse pairs such as economic and economical.
